verse1.philosophical_explanation: Bhagavad Gita Chapter 14 Verse 1 offers a layered teaching on disciplined action, inner clarity, and God-centered wisdom, presenting dharma as a harmonizing principle that integrates duty, knowledge, devotion, and self-mastery. In Vedantic reflection, the outer event is never merely external; it mirrors the inner field of the seeker where attachment, fear, pride, compassion, and discernment contend for dominance. The text therefore asks the reader to cultivate viveka, sustained discrimination between the permanent and the impermanent, while remaining active in righteous responsibilities. It also emphasizes that true strength is not aggression but alignment with satya, ahimsa in intent, self-restraint, and surrender to the Divine will. Ethical life in Sanatana Dharma emerges through disciplined action offered without egoic possessiveness, where one performs svadharma with humility and accountability. This teaching is socially relevant because it links personal transformation with collective order: families, communities, and governance remain stable only when conduct is rooted in justice, gratitude, and reverence for truth. Spiritually, the section invites bhakti and contemplative awareness, showing that liberation-oriented living can begin within ordinary duties when the heart is purified through right understanding and service.
verse1.scripture_text: श्रीभगवानुवाच | परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् | यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ||१४-१||

verse.sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् | यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ||१४-१||
verse.translation: 14.1 The Blessed Lord said I will again declare (to thee) that supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledge, having known which all the sages have gone to the supreme perfection after this life.
verse.transliteration: śrībhagavānuvāca . paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānamuttamam . yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ ||14-1||

verse.translation: 14.6 Of these, Sattva, which from its stainlessness is luminous and healthy, binds by attachment to happiness and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.
verse.transliteration: tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam . sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha ||14-6||

verse7.philosophical_explanation: Bhagavad Gita Chapter 14 Verse 7 offers a layered teaching on disciplined action, inner clarity, and God-centered wisdom, presenting dharma as a harmonizing principle that integrates duty, knowledge, devotion, and self-mastery. In Vedantic reflection, the outer event is never merely external; it mirrors the inner field of the seeker where attachment, fear, pride, compassion, and discernment contend for dominance. The text therefore asks the reader to cultivate viveka, sustained discrimination between the permanent and the impermanent, while remaining active in righteous responsibilities. It also emphasizes that true strength is not aggression but alignment with satya, ahimsa in intent, self-restraint, and surrender to the Divine will. Ethical life in Sanatana Dharma emerges through disciplined action offered without egoic possessiveness, where one performs svadharma with humility and accountability. This teaching is socially relevant because it links personal transformation with collective order: families, communities, and governance remain stable only when conduct is rooted in justice, gratitude, and reverence for truth. Spiritually, the section invites bhakti and contemplative awareness, showing that liberation-oriented living can begin within ordinary duties when the heart is purified through right understanding and service.
verse7.scripture_text: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् | तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ||१४-७||

verse.sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् | तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ||१४-७||
verse.translation: 14.7 Know thou Rajas to be of the nature of passion, the source of thirst (for sensual enjoyment) and attachment; it binds fast, O Arjuna, the embodied one by attachment to action.
verse.transliteration: rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam . tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam ||14-7||

verse.translation: 14.9 Sattva attaches to happiness, Rajas to action, O Arjuna, while Tamas verily shrouding knowledge attaches to heedlessness.
